intent_en: Dewi's high-income household has far greater access to clean water than Putri's low-income household, showing that income inequality extends to basic services.
previous_intent: To illustrate the disparity in access to clean water, contrasting the near-universal availability in developed contexts (exemplified by Dewey's upbringing) with the lower global average.
narration_support: Dewey grew up in a house with clean running water and a toilet.
chart_support: A split-screen graphic comparing access to clean water, displaying a significantly higher access rate on the left side (visually represented by higher water levels) than on the right side.
evidence_note: The narration is sparse (single sentence) but establishes a baseline of high access. The chart provides the statistical comparison of access to clean water between two groups (implied 98% vs 72% visually, described qualitatively to adhere to rules).
sequence_context: Across this sequence, household income inequality places Dewi's family far above Putri's, translates into unequal access to clean water, and affects a broader low-income population than the poorest decile alone.
